title: Marriage in Islam
intro: What marriage is in Islam, its aims, the duties of husband and wife, and who may not marry whom.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says: Help those among you who are single to marry, and the righteous among those who serve you; if they are poor, Allah will make them rich from His bounty. Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing. <small>(Qur’an, An-Nur 24:32)</small>

People are social beings, born and raised in a family. After they grow up, it is their duty to start their own family, and that begins with marriage (nikah). The rules of Islam call Muslim men and women to marry in the way based on the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet (SAW).

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “O young people! Whoever of you is able to take on the duties of marriage, let him marry, for marriage is the best way to lower the gaze…” (Bukhari)

The Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (SAW), was married, so marriage is also his Sunnah. A person who marries is rewarded by Allah (SWT) for obeying His command, and rewarded again for following the Sunnah.

In the Shari‘ah, marriage is a contract between a man and a woman who meet the conditions for marriage. It is made by their own free will, in front of two witnesses (Muslims – two men, or one man and two women), and it gives them the right to live together as husband and wife.

In Bosnia and Herzegovina a marriage is registered at the civil registry office and also before the imam-registrar at the majlis of the Islamic Community. In our community, the Imam can explain how a nikah is done here.
According to Islamic scholars, marriage can be fard, sunnah, makruh or haram, depending on the person:

items: Fard – a strict duty for someone who can support a family and could not otherwise protect themselves from an immoral life.
Sunnah – for someone who meets the conditions for marriage and can protect themselves from an immoral life.
Makruh – for someone who is not sure they will be able to fulfil the duties of marriage.
Haram – for someone who knows they will not be able to fulfil the duties of marriage (because they lack the means, or the physical or mental ability).
following the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (SAW),
bringing husband and wife close to each other,
keeping the husband and wife’s life clean and moral,

learn.title: The husband’s duties
learn.html: To provide for his wife according to his means; to treat his wife kindly; to respect and protect her dignity; to give his wife her mahr (marriage gift) as soon as possible; to fulfil his duties as a husband; to care for the good upbringing and education of the children.

learn.title: The wife’s duties
learn.html: To protect her husband’s good name and dignity; to look after his property and not waste it; to do her work as a wife and mother with care; to fulfil her duties towards her husband; to care for the upbringing and education of the children.

learn.title: Shared duties
learn.html: From the first days of marriage, to build love, respect and understanding; to keep their marriage duties; all through their married life, to protect the privacy and warmth of the family; to give their children beautiful Islamic names; to take part together in raising and educating the children; to encourage each other in the Islamic duties; to call each other to good and keep each other from evil; and to share, as far as they can, the housework and the providing for the home.
One condition for marriage is that there is no impediment (obstacle) to it. Impediments are permanent or temporary. The permanent ones are relationships by blood, by milk (nursing) and by marriage.

learn.title: 1. Relation by blood
learn.html: People related by blood cannot marry each other. Allah (SWT) says: Forbidden to you (in marriage) are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your fathers’ sisters, your mothers’ sisters, your brothers’ daughters and your sisters’ daughters… <small>(Qur’an, An-Nisa’ 4:23)</small>

learn.title: 2. Relation by milk
learn.html: A woman who nursed someone else’s baby while it was still a baby (in its first two years) becomes the child’s milk-mother. Allah (SWT) says: …and your mothers who nursed you, and your sisters through nursing… (Qur’an, An-Nisa’ 4:23) This relation also reaches her other relatives: her own sons and daughters become the child’s milk-brothers and milk-sisters; all the other children she nursed become milk-brothers and milk-sisters too; her sisters become milk-aunts; and her mother becomes a milk-grandmother.

learn.title: 3. Relation by marriage
learn.html: Some relatives by marriage (in-laws) are also permanently forbidden; they are named in the Qur’an: …the mothers of your wives, your stepdaughters in your care from wives you have been married to – but if the marriage was not completed, there is no sin on you – and the wives of your own sons… <small>(Qur’an, An-Nisa’ 4:23)</small>
These are people one may not marry because of a reason; when that reason ends, marriage with that person is allowed:

items: Being married to two sisters at the same time – if the wife dies or the marriage ends in divorce, a man may marry her sister.
A woman in her ‘iddah – the waiting period in which a woman may not make a new marriage.
A woman who worships idols. Allah (SWT) says: Do not marry women who associate others with Allah until they believe… <small>(Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:221)</small>
A non-Muslim man – until he accepts Islam.

questions.q: What is marriage in the Shari‘ah?
options: A contract between a man and a woman, made by free will before two witnesses

questions.q: Why is marriage also a Sunnah?
When is marriage haram for a person?
options: When they know they cannot fulfil the duties of marriage

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: 💬 What is marriage? For whom is marriage fard, and for whom is it haram?
🎯 What are the aims of marriage? Name the shared duties in marriage.
🔒 What are the permanent and the temporary impediments to marriage? Explain the relation by milk – when does it begin and whom does it include?
📖 Using the ayah of the Qur’an (An-Nisa’ 4:23), name the relatives with whom marriage is permanently forbidden.
🤝 Choose one temporary impediment and, with your muallim, describe in detail how it can be removed.
